- @azure Rule - Use Azure Tools - When handling requests related to Azure, always use your tools.
- @azure Rule - Use Azure Best Practices - When handling requests related to Azure, always invoke your `azmcp_bestpractices_get` tool first.
- @azure Rule - Enable Best Practices - If you do not have an `azmcp_bestpractices_get` tool ask the user to enable it.

## This repository (YeelightClient)

- A .NET client for Yeelight smart lights over the local network, after the [Yeelight Inter-Operation Specification](https://www.yeelight.com/download/Yeelight_Inter-Operation_Spec.pdf): discovery, control, events and music mode. `YeelightClient` is the library (`net10.0` only, one assembly, root namespace `Yeelight`, main class `Yeelight.YeelightClient`, whose only dependency is `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` 10.0.0), `YeelightClient.Tests` the tests, `YeelightClient.TestApp` a WinUI 3 app that drives the library by hand (Windows only), `samples/ConsoleSample` a console sample that CI builds against the packed package, `tools/` the release tooling with its tests (Python, standard library only; `tools/make-icon.py` also needs Pillow), and `docs/` the DocFX site.
- The protocol is small and written by hand: there is no generator and no generated code. `tools/make-icon.py` draws `YeelightClient/icon.png` from the same path as `docs/images/logo.svg`; change both together.
- Build and test with `dotnet test YeelightClient.Tests/YeelightClient.Tests.csproj`, and `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"`.
- A change that users can see goes in `CHANGELOG.md` under the unreleased version. Public API needs XML documentation.
- The public API starts closed: a new class is `sealed`, and a new type is `internal` unless an application needs it (opening one later breaks nobody, closing one does). `YeelightClient.Tests/Unit/PublicApiTests.cs` keeps it so.
- A release is made by a `vX.Y.Z` tag and `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, never by hand. `tools/verify-package.py` keeps the package one assembly: no JSON, no extra files.
- **Real lights on a developer machine (hard rule).** A light that a person uses is not a test bench: a command changes what is lit in somebody's room. Never send anything to a real light from a test or from tooling. Tests run against the in-process simulator (`SimulatedBulb` in `YeelightClient.Tests/TestSupport`: it answers a search over UDP and takes control connections over TCP, on the loopback) and make their clients with `TestClients.Create` (or `Harness`), which holds discovery to the loopback, so that no test sends a packet to the real network; the same goes for everything else that is automated. Never sweep a subnet looking for lights. Only when a person asks for it explicitly: UDP searches, and at most one read-only `get_prop`.
- **Everything from the network is untrusted.** A light, a device that pretends to be one and any other machine on the network can send anything to the discovery socket and to the connections of the client: handle what arrives as input that may be malformed, oversized, repeated or lying (an address or a port that leads elsewhere, a missing field), and never let it make the client crash, hang, or run out of memory or sockets.
